29: 
30: module test_infrstrct_fifo
31: #(
32:     parameter BIT_WIDTH     = 64,   // data width 
33:     parameter ENTRIES       = 16,   // number of entries in the FIFP
34:     parameter LOG2_ENTRIES  = 4     // log base 2 of number of entries in FIFO
35: )
36: (
37:     input                       clk,
38:     input                       rst_n,
39: 
40:     input [BIT_WIDTH-1:0]       din,
41:     input                       wr_en,
42:     input                       rd_en,
43: 
44:     output reg [BIT_WIDTH-1:0]  dout,
45:     output reg                  full,
46:     output reg                  empty,
47:     output reg                  val  
48: );
49: 
50:     //
51:     // Signal Declarations
52:     //
53: 
54:     // FIFO memory
55:     reg [BIT_WIDTH-1:0]         m_f[ENTRIES-1:0];
56:     reg [BIT_WIDTH-1:0]         m_next;
57:     integer                     i;
58: 
59:     // Pointer variables
60:     reg [LOG2_ENTRIES-1:0]      wr_pointer_f;
61:     reg [LOG2_ENTRIES-1:0]      wr_pointer_next;
62:     reg [LOG2_ENTRIES-1:0]      rd_pointer_f;
63:     reg [LOG2_ENTRIES-1:0]      rd_pointer_next;
64: 
65:     // Entry count variables
66:     reg [LOG2_ENTRIES:0]        entry_count_f;
67:     reg [LOG2_ENTRIES:0]        entry_count_next;
68: 
69:     //
70:     // Synchronous logic
71:     //
72:     
73:     // All flip-flops
74:     always @ (posedge clk)
75:     begin
76:         if (~rst_n)
77:         begin
78:             wr_pointer_f        <= 0;
79:             rd_pointer_f        <= 0;
80:             entry_count_f       <= 0;
81:             for (i = 0; i < ENTRIES; i = i + 1)
82:                 m_f[i] <= 0;
83:         end
84:         else
85:         begin
86:             wr_pointer_f        <= wr_pointer_next;
87:             rd_pointer_f        <= rd_pointer_next;
88:             entry_count_f       <= entry_count_next;
89:             m_f[wr_pointer_f]   <= m_next;
90:         end
91:     end
92:     
93:     //
94:     // Combinational logic
95:     // 
96: 
97:     // Write and read pointers
98:     always @ *
99:     begin
100:         wr_pointer_next = wr_pointer_f;
101:         rd_pointer_next = rd_pointer_f;
102:         if (wr_en)
103:             wr_pointer_next = wr_pointer_f + 1;
104:         if (rd_en && val)
105:             rd_pointer_next = rd_pointer_f + 1;
106:     end
107: 
108:     // Write logic
109:     always @ *
110:     begin
111:         m_next = m_f[wr_pointer_f];
112:         if (wr_en)
113:             m_next = din;
114:     end
115: 
116:     // Output data and valid signal
117:     always @ *
118:     begin
119:         // Take care of case where we are writing and reading
120:         // on the same cycle to the same location
121:         if (rd_en && wr_en && rd_pointer_f == wr_pointer_f)
122:         begin
123:             dout = din;
124:             val = 1'b1;
125:         end
126:         else
127:         begin
128:             dout = m_f[rd_pointer_f];
129:             val = rd_en && ~empty;
130:         end
131:     end
132: 
133:     // Entry count
134:     always @ *
135:     begin
136:         entry_count_next = entry_count_f;
137:         if (rd_en && !wr_en && (entry_count_f != 0))
138:             entry_count_next = entry_count_f - 1;
139:         else if (!rd_en && wr_en && (entry_count_f != ENTRIES))
140:             entry_count_next = entry_count_f + 1;
141:     end
142: 
143:     // Full/empty logic
144:     always @ *
145:     begin
146:         full = (entry_count_f == (ENTRIES-1));
147:         empty = (entry_count_f == 0);
148:     end
